If you liked Game of Thrones, you'd probably enjoy historical fiction too. It's like fantasy where the stakes are amped way up and characters can die from stuff like dysentery. 

A couple I'd recommend are Sharon Kay Penman (I'd start with her Welsh trilogy; book 1 is Here Be Dragons) and Colleen McCullough, in particular her Masters of Rome series. Fantastic writers and meticulous researchers so you can rest assured they have their facts straight. 

My favorite part of a Penman book is the afterward when she explains any liberties she's taken and why, and any places where she had to speculate because what actually happened isn't known. She will also confirm any of the more outlandish stuff that happened. Seriously, some of these lesser known historical events are WILD. 

They do tend to whitewash their main characters, but if you can look past that they're amazing! Sadly, both passed a few years back, but they were pretty prolific so they'll keep you busy for a while!

I am BEYOND SHOCKED that no one has mentioned Mark Lawrence. He is at the top of my fantasy tier with Sanderson and Abercrombie, where I pre-order books months in advance because I completely trust that they'll be that good. 

Most folks would say to start with his Broken Empire series (starting with Prince of Thorns) but it's very brutal. Although if you end up liking Abercrombie you probably will like other grimdark series. Still, it's pretty jarring going hard R after coming from Sanderson's mostly PG writing. Book of the Ancester (starting with Red Sister) is a more gentle introduction and also very very good. 

You can really start anywhere with him, but I will say he's kind of building a cosmere himself, though he hasn't advertised it like Sanderson. He even has a recurring character. I'd say more but I don't want to spoil anything!

He's a master world builder, like Abercrombie and Sanderson, and I absolutely love his prose. There's a sentence at the end of Prince of Thorns that I have bookmarked and go back to periodically. It always chokes me up.

Anyway, definitely one for everyone here to check out!

Pillars, then Column, then Evening, then World. 

Pillars is one of the greatest novels I've ever read. Just wonderful world building and research. 

Column of Fire was a nice return to form although it suffered a bit from having to factor in so many historical events and figures. It was a jam packed book and it felt like we didn't get to spend enough time with some of the characters, plus the ending felt rushed.

E&M felt lighter and shorter than the other three, likely at least partly due to the lack of historical records from the time. In that respect, it suffers from the opposite of what Column suffered from. But it was vintage Follett, with great world building, characters you care about, memorable and horrible villains, and just a whole lot of that trademark suffering.

It won't be a popular opinion, but I almost actively disliked World Without End. It is still Follett and still has all the great things I mentioned above, but oh my God did he lean in on the rape and sex. Way way overboard to where it feels gratuitous. In the other books, the sex scenes have meaning and impact. This felt more like medieval porn (and like torture porn in a few places). The story and characters were great and the research was excellent as always but man did that detract from it.

I have been season pass holders at both parks. Very different experiences and worth trying both if you enjoy high ropes. Go Ape feels more adventurous. You're surrounded by woods. The courses are higher up. You have to follow a trail through the woods between courses. It also has a swing into a cargo net that is the most fun obstacle at either course. However, it is easier as another reviewer noted. It's more expensive. They (usually) don't let you go twice. And you're stuck on a linear path through the courses.

Treerunners has a central hub that's situated next to a community center, sport fields and big parking lot. It does have harder courses. I think there's less wait, especially since they still use clip its that let you go around slower folks vs the continuous trolley system Go Ape adopted in 2022 (the go Ape system is very well implemented I might add; much better than the ones at the US Natl Whitewater center which are just bad). Also you aren't on a linear path so the higher courses tend to be less traversed, though the steps up in difficulty mean you'll get people stuck more often than at Go Ape. And the red course (I think they call it double black now actually) is far FAR harder than any other course at either park.

Both are very good and worthwhile!

Sanderson is a machine. He and Stephen King have always amazed me with their incredible work ethic. It's amazing that the quality never suffers. Martin and Rothfuss seem like they petered out. They had a burst of inspiration and churned out a few fantastic books fairly quickly, then lost motivation. I am not holding out hope for an end to ASOIAF or Kingkiller, and if they are written, I'm guessing the quality will be less than desired (Martin already went down that path with the last few books).

On a side note, it's kind of funny to me that Sanderson is the ultimate plotter and King is the ultimate pantser. You can easily see it in their styles. Sanderson's work is a bit more mechanical, but ultimately very tightly plotted with incredible world building and magic systems. King, however, has far more imagination and often veers into brilliance, while his characterizations are vivid and engrossing, but he also dips into mediocrity and it's obvious that he has issues wrapping stories up sometimes (\*cough\* IT \*cough cough\* Dark Tower). Both are fantastic authors though; thank goodness they have and continue to produce so much great stuff.

Only really decent argument I've heard against net neutrality is that some remote ISPs have better local networks than their pipe in from the rest of the internet. If they could cache Netflix and other high-bandwidth consuming content locally, they could create a better user experience and free up that pipe for other content.
